title: A finite fraction chart with proper principal extended maximal ideal
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a nonzero local integral domain, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B
e0$. Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] containing $B$ such that every element of $K$ is $b/c$ with $b,c\in B$ and $c
e0$. There exist an integer $r\ge1$, nonzero elements $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in\mathfrak m_B$ generating $\mathfrak m_B$, and an index $j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ such that, for $a=x_j$, the subring $S=B[x_1/a,\ldots,x_r/a]\subseteq K$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak m_BS=aS
e S$. Here $B[x_1/a,\ldots,x_r/a]$ consists of polynomial expressions in the indicated field quotients with coefficients in $B$, and $\mathfrak m_BS$ is the ideal of $S$ generated by $\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof from choosing a dominating valuation ring through S contained in A and x_r S not equal to S (original item steps 1-3 and properness part of step 4).

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose finitely many generators of $\mathfrak m_B$. Delete zero generators. The remaining list $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ is nonempty since $\mathfrak m_B\ne0$, so $r\ge1$ and each $x_i\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof through the construction of S and the assertion x_r S is proper

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] to the local subring $B\subseteq K$. Obtain a valuation ring $V\subseteq K$ containing $B$ with $B\cap\mathfrak m_V=\mathfrak m_B$. In particular each $x_i$ belongs to $\mathfrak m_V$.

source.place: Tag 00IA, lemma-dominate; invoked in Tag 00P8, first sentence of proof

proof.text: Using the fraction-field condition of [def-trf-valuation-ring], select a generator $a=x_j$ dividing all the generators in $V$, as follows. Start with $a=x_1$. On adjoining the next generator $x_i$, either $x_i/a\in V$, in which case keep $a$, or $a/x_i\in V$, in which case replace $a$ by $x_i$. Every previous quotient $x_h/a$ then becomes $(x_h/a)(a/x_i)=x_h/x_i\in V$. Finite induction gives $x_i/a\in V$ for all $i$, with $a$ still a nonzero member of the original list.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof through the construction of S and the assertion x_r S is proper

proof.text: Put $S=B[x_1/a,\ldots,x_r/a]\subseteq K$. Since $B\subseteq V$ and every indicated quotient belongs to $V$, closure under sums and products gives $S\subseteq V$. Each generator $x_i=a(x_i/a)$ lies in $aS$, hence $\mathfrak m_BS\subseteq aS$. Conversely $a\in\mathfrak m_B$ gives $aS\subseteq\mathfrak m_BS$. Thus $\mathfrak m_BS=aS$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof through the construction of S and the assertion x_r S is proper

proof.text: Because $a=x_j\in\mathfrak m_V$ and $S\subseteq V$, the equality $aS=S$ would give $1=as\in\mathfrak m_V$ for some $s\in S$, impossible for a proper maximal ideal. Therefore $aS\ne S$.

source.place: Tag 00P8, lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1, proof through the construction of S and the assertion x_r S is proper

proof.text: The evaluation homomorphism $B[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to S$, $T_i\mapsto x_i/a$, is surjective by the definition of $S$ as polynomial expressions. The quotient by its kernel is $S$: the map $[P]\mapsto P(x_1/a,\ldots,x_r/a)$ is well-defined and bijective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to this finite type $B$-algebra and the given Noetherian ring $B$. It follows that $S$ is Noetherian, completing all the assertions.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, first assertion; applied to the finite chart in Tag 00P8
